title: Back and forward, app-wide
steps: Open a few notes from the list on the left: Chores, then Shopping, then This week. Press the browser's Back button: Shopping, then Chores, each where the cursor was. Forward goes the other way. The mouse's side buttons and a trackpad swipe do the same.
⌘[ and ⌘] (Ctrl-[ and Ctrl-] elsewhere), or Go back and Go forward in ⌘⇧P, move through the same places, and the browser's Back and Forward stay in step with them.
Split the window (⌘\), open a note on the right, then go back: focus returns to the left window and the note it showed. A window you've closed since: its notes open in the window you're in.
Open a note from the list, then another: the second takes the first's preview tab. Go back: the first comes back in the preview tab.

In Vim, G jumps to the end of a note, and Ctrl-O comes back to where you were; Ctrl-I goes forward again. Ctrl-O and Ctrl-I are Go back and Go forward, through notes and windows too, as VSCodeVim does. Moving the cursor a few lines isn't a place of its own: only jumps are.
Reload the page: you're where you were, and Back still goes back.
Settings, Workbench, Navigation arrows: ← and → at the start of the top left tab bar. Off by default.
